title: Older-Adult Fall Injury Prevention And Post-Fall Function In Low- And Middle-Income Countries
summary: Build a verified measurement workflow for older-adult falls in low- and middle-income countries that separates event incidence, injury severity, time-to-care, rehabilitation access, functional recovery, prevention fidelity, and equity before any scale-up decision.
why_it_matters: A Ministry of Health healthy-ageing or injury-prevention director, a district health authority, or a development funder must decide whether to finance community fall prevention, safer-home work, injury surveillance, emergency referral, fracture care, or rehabilitation capacity. WHO estimates 684,000 fatal falls and 37.3 million falls requiring medical attention each year, with over 80% of fall-related fatalities in low- and middle-income countries and the highest death rates among adults over 60 (evidence: who-falls-global-burden-2021). A six-country nationally representative SAGE analysis found a 4.0% pooled prevalence of self-reported past-year fall-related injury among adults aged 50 years and older, while a prospective registry across 23 facilities in Malawi and Tanzania found long arrival delays and substantial differences between facility populations (evidence: sage-fall-injury-lmic-2015, sawe-fall-registry-malawi-tanzania-2023). A rural-China cluster trial shows that an integrated primary-care fall-prevention programme can be evaluated, but not that its effect transports to other settings (evidence: family-fall-prevention-rct-china-2025). A verified country-level cascade from fall to function could change a real prevention, referral, rehabilitation, or data-system allocation; it must not become an individual risk score, treatment order, or universal intervention recommendation without domain, red-team, field-reality, and independent replication review.

success_metrics.target: Every estimate records the fall definition, age band, setting, recall or observation window, case-finding source, recurrence rule, injury threshold, numerator, denominator, sampling frame, and missingness; facility presentations are not treated as population incidence.
success_metrics.validation_method: A replicator reconstructs the event denominator from the cited source methods and blocks comparisons when definitions, catchment, recall, or case-finding are incompatible.

success_metrics.target: Every setting separates fall occurrence, injury severity, transport, time-to-care, facility assessment, admission, surgery or fracture care, transfer, rehabilitation, functional outcome, and death.
success_metrics.validation_method: A health-systems reviewer traces each pathway field to a source or timestamped record and records whether it observes the population, the facility, or the patient episode.

success_metrics.target: Any prevention result reports allocation, cluster or participant eligibility, intervention components, exposure or attendance, co-interventions, follow-up, attrition, and prespecified fall and functional outcomes.
success_metrics.validation_method: An independent replicator reruns the reported effect calculation and checks that self-reported falls and functional measures are not silently substituted for one another.

success_metrics.target: Every output preserves age, sex, rurality, poverty, disability, living arrangement, home and work setting, transport access, language, consent, refusal, and safeguarding fields where relevant.
success_metrics.validation_method: A field-reality and red-team review checks that risk factors are not converted into blame, exclusion, coercive home access, or automated denial of care.

success_metrics.target: No fall-prevention, fracture-care, rehabilitation, or resource-allocation recommendation advances beyond measurement framing without domain review, red-team review, field-reality review, and independent replication.
success_metrics.validation_method: Review records, input hashes, and replication results are checked before any country-facing or operational output is published.

review_policy.merge_gate: Schema validation, injury-prevention and health-systems domain review, red-team review for clinical, home-safety, medication, and targeting overreach, field-reality review for prevention and care pathways, and independent replication before any quantitative or operational recommendation.
